methodological_questions: Does a teammate DRIVE immediately before a PNR raise next-possession PNR PPP relative to a matched comparison?
Are DRIVE and PNR labels valid enough to define the preceding-DRIVE sequence without outcome-dependent misclassification?
Can foul endings, low-confidence labels, and proxy-calibrated PNR labels be separated from real efficiency?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type labeling audit found OTHER possessions with 36% foul endings and inflated PPP; DRIVE 12pp below the foul benchmark; PNR foul rate 22%; only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapped to a real play type via initiation_type.

Play-type label accuracy/distribution audit recorded overall FAIL (verdict tool_eval_fail): OTHER 20.2% vs <10% target, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% vs 14-22% benchmark, most play types above PPP band, MIA identity checks failed.

Backfilled label verification: PNR share 28.7% FAIL (band 20-28%), PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL, 3100 games with team PNR >33% FAIL, PNR PPP 0.948 PASS, temporal PASS, team identity FAIL; 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated; final FAIL on 921,514 possessions.
2024-25 shot-level PNR share of half-court shots ranged from 7.567% (OKC) to 13.824% (IND); used as calibration input for PBPProxyPNR; no pass/fail gate recorded.
On-ball coverage labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) reached 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60) labeled; switches_on unpopulated; verdict failed_gate.

Season stability of top suppressors: 2/30 stars stable (>=75%). Negative teammate pairs recorded include Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR -0.263 (n=31) and Tatum->Porzingis DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.444 (n=31). Verdict null, described as adequately powered.
Opponent play before a star's possession: PUTBACK top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g., Mitchell d=-0.294, n_after=95); no multiplicity correction; several cells n=32-95.
PUTBACK suppression via fatigue (H1 -0.038 vs H2 -0.130); Q4 pooled n=34 is sparse. Concerns PUTBACK, not DRIVE->PNR.

Star suppression by lineup and forced play type (e.g., Giannis forced PULL_UP 0.848 vs preferred DRIVE, largest gap); no placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
A1 adaptation falsification: wrong-way teams gap and carryover tests; T3 next-game PPP Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842; classified artifact (C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Taking play-type PPP differences at face value as efficiency
failed_approaches.why: Foul-ending possessions inflated OTHER PPP; DRIVE and PNR shares diverged from foul benchmarks; initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred play-type labels for adaptation and sequence findings
failed_approaches.why: Audit overall FAIL with systematic label issues, foul leakage into OTHER, and identity-check failures.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Backfilled PNR labels as analysis input
failed_approaches.why: Band and team-identity checks failed; 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy-calibrated, not directly observed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive scheme from matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rates 14.9% and 3.3%; switches_on not populated; failed_gate.
Only 2/30 stars met the stability rule (rejected; adequately powered null per record).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Opponent-before-star suppression as a reliable effect
failed_approaches.why: No multiplicity correction; cells with n_after 32-95 against thousands of baseline possessions.
Placebo dependence; star-chain gaps later treated as artifacts; mechanism unclear.

evidence_establishes: The play-type labels in this data pipeline have repeatedly failed validity checks (FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-CHT-025), so any sequence analysis built on them inherits label risk.
PNR labels are largely proxy-calibrated rather than directly observed in the prior backfill (82.8%, FAM:SF-APPA-030).

Earlier sequential-suppression and teammate-pair analyses on this data were either not hypothesis tests, rejected for stability, or flagged as artifacts; none tested the DRIVE-to-PNR premium under a validated design.

One retrieved record reports a negative DRIVE->PNR teammate-pair premium (Giannis->Lillard -0.263, n=31) inside a stability analysis that found almost no stable sequential effects (FAM:SF-APPA-058). This is the only retrieved record touching the exact DRIVE->PNR pair, and it runs opposite to the hypothesis.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a teammate DRIVE raises PNR PPP. No retrieved record estimated this contrast with a validated DRIVE label, a matched comparison, and a valid PNR label.
The size or sign of the DRIVE->PNR premium in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data, given that the record covering that pair (FAM:SF-APPA-058) is itself a small-n cell and was not designed to test it.
Whether the PNR PPP 0.948 PASS in FAM:SF-APPA-030 reflects valid PNR possessions, since the same family failed the share and identity checks.
Any validated estimate for 2025-26, since that season is partial before 2026-04-13 and the playoff season is partial before 2026-06-21.
own_inferences: The question is a sequential contrast requiring a reliable preceding-action label (teammate DRIVE) and a reliable outcome label (PNR possession) on the same possession chain. The retrieved evidence says both label sets have failed validity checks on this data.
Because the hypothesis is an upward premium, foul-ending possessions and proxy-calibrated PNR labels could create spurious positive gaps, consistent with the artifact pattern in FAM:SF-CHT-025.
The one record covering the DRIVE->PNR pair shows a negative value, which suggests the sign of the effect is not settled by existing work and that the proposed direction is at least uncertain.
A test on pre-2025-26 data with label validation gates could be feasible, but only after the label audit passes.
uncertainties: The record for FAM:SF-APPA-058 does not state how the 'Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR' pair is directionally defined (which player is the DRIVE actor), so the sign is not interpretable without re-reading the family.
The units of PNR PPP 0.948 in FAM:SF-APPA-030 are not specified in the record.
The retrieval did not return any record that defines a labeled DRIVE-preceding-PNR sequence or its sample size.
The audit results are from earlier pipeline versions; current label quality is not recorded.
No validation status is recorded for any family (all 'no_validation_recorded').

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved label-audit families (FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-CHT-025) show the play-type labels fail validity and foul-leakage checks, so a direct test of DRIVE->PNR PPP cannot proceed now. Prior sequence work (FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-CHT-009) also shows that similar sequential claims were rejected, unvalidated, or artifacts. The decision moves from a possible direct test to do_not_proceed until the label gate is passed.

blocking_constraints.text: DRIVE and PNR labels failed validity audits (FAM:SF-APPM-014 FAIL; FAM:SF-APPA-030 FAIL; 82.8% PNR proxy-calibrated; initiation_type mapped only 0.7%).
Possession-level play types and PPP are both derived from the same play-by-play, so the label and the outcome are coupled.
Lineup, defender matchup, score margin, clock, and foul endings all plausibly co-vary with DRIVE-preceded PNRs and PPP.
Retrieved cells with n=20-95 (FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF-APPA-050) show power is limited for team-by-player sequence cells; the power for the league-wide contrast has not been computed.
Earlier sequence claims without placebo (FAM:SF-CHT-009) were later treated as artifacts, so placebo checks are required.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the teammate DRIVE->PNR PPP premium under validated labels. Retrieved work includes label audits that failed (FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-CHT-025), sequence-suppression analyses that were rejected, unvalidated, or flagged as artifacts (FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-CHT-009), and one negative DRIVE->PNR pair value inside a stability analysis (FAM:SF-APPA-058). This is adjacent evidence, not an answer.

risks.text: Play-type and initiator labels failed audits; foul endings leak into OTHER and DRIVE; PNR labels are proxy-calibrated.
Preceding-DRIVE and PNR labels are both built from the same play-by-play used to compute PPP.
Lineup, defender, score state, pace, and rotation effects are not controlled in the retrieved designs.
Sequence cells in retrieved families were n=20-95; the teammate-pair cell (n=31) is too small for a reliable premium estimate.
Retrieved sequence work tested many player-pair and play-type pairs without correction (FAM:SF-APPA-050).
Sequence gaps without placebo were later classed as artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Teammate DRIVE immediately before PNR may be rare, so the preceded-PNR cell may be small even league-wide; not computed.
Earlier analyses spanned seasons with changing play-type coding and team identities; 2025-26 is partial in both regular season and playoffs.
Derived records may use full-game information; the preceding-action label must be defined using only information available before the PNR.

design.estimand: Within-team, within-game difference in next-possession PNR PPP when the immediately preceding possession is a teammate DRIVE versus a matched non-DRIVE teammate action, with the PNR ball-handler and defensive matchup held fixed. This is a conditional contrast, not a causal effect.
design.unit: PNR possession, linked to the immediately preceding possession in the same game and period.
design.sample: Regular season and playoffs for 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 only, after a passed label audit. Exclude 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, which are partial at the 2026-06-14 snapshot. Use a fixed data snapshot.
design.power: Not computed. Before running, compute the minimum detectable PPP difference at 80% power for the expected count of DRIVE->PNR pairs. Retrieved cell sizes (n=20-95) suggest the league-wide cell must be checked; if it falls below the minimum detectable effect, the test is underpowered and should not be run.
design.controls: Lineup and on-court personnel, defender matchup, score margin, game clock and shot clock buckets, period, team and season fixed effects, exclusion of foul-ending possessions, and restriction to labels with confidence above a pre-set threshold. PNR labels must be directly observed, not proxy-calibrated.
design.falsification: (a) Placebo: opposing-team DRIVE preceding PNR, which should show no premium if the effect is teammate-specific. (b) Lagged placebo: DRIVE two possessions earlier. (c) Label-quality placebo: rerun on possessions with low-confidence labels to check whether the premium tracks label noise. A premium that appears equally in placebo cells is treated as an artifact.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single primary contrast. Any additional play-type pairs are exploratory and corrected with Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg across the full pre-specified family.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to an estimate only if (1) the label audit passes on the sample (play-type shares within benchmark bands, foul-ending leakage under the pre-set threshold, and no proxy-calibrated PNR labels in the primary cell); (2) the minimum detectable effect is at or below the smallest effect of substantive interest; and (3) placebo contrasts show no comparable premium. Otherwise, report as untestable or artifact, not as a positive or null result.
design.data_version: Frozen snapshot of 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular-season and playoff play-by-play, rotation intervals, starters, matchup minutes, and box scores, recorded with the snapshot date and a hash. Exclude 2025-26 partial data. Label-derivation code version pinned and documented.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
